name: MCP OAuth 2.1
summary: The MCP specification's authorization layer for HTTP servers. The MCP server is an OAuth 2.1 resource server; the client discovers the authorization server through Protected Resource Metadata, registers, runs an authorization-code flow with PKCE, and sends audience-bound bearer tokens.
facts: Client ID Metadata Documents preferred; Dynamic Client Registration deprecated
Optional; HTTP transports only, stdio uses environment credentials
goodFor: Remote MCP servers acting for a signed-in user
Per-user, revocable, scoped access instead of shared keys
watchOut: Several spec revisions in a year; older clients may only do DCR
Each server needs an authorization server behind it
